subsystems.name: Reconnaissance and attack-surface mapping
subsystems.role: builds a picture of what is exposed before anything is attacked.

subsystems.name: Planner and orchestrator
subsystems.role: the reasoning loop that decides what to try next and keeps track of what has been learned.
parts: large language model planner with tool calling
memory store of findings and failed attempts

subsystems.name: Exploit engine
subsystems.role: turns a suspected weakness into a working, repeatable attack.
parts: exploit chaining across hosts and accounts

subsystems.name: Sandbox and target replica
subsystems.role: a disposable copy of the target where attacks can be run without harming anything real.

subsystems.name: Verification and reporting
subsystems.role: separates genuine exploitable flaws from plausible-looking noise.

subsystems.name: Guardrails and authorisation
subsystems.role: keeps an autonomous attacker inside the agreed scope.
parts: kill switch and human approval gates

buildSteps.title: Agree scope and authorisation
buildSteps.detail: Write rules of engagement naming exactly which hosts, accounts and time windows may be touched, and which techniques are forbidden — without this, none of the rest is legal.

buildSteps.title: Clone the target environment
buildSteps.detail: Stand up an isolated replica: the same services, versions and configurations, with no route to production or the public internet, and snapshotting so any state can be rewound in seconds.

buildSteps.title: Expose tools as callable actions
buildSteps.detail: Install scanners, fuzzers, debuggers and exploitation frameworks inside the sandbox and wrap each one in a structured interface with typed arguments and parsed output.

buildSteps.title: Wire the agent loop
buildSteps.detail: Connect an LLM to that tool interface with a plan–act–observe cycle: propose an action, run it, read the result, update the findings graph, decide again.

buildSteps.title: Ground it in vulnerability knowledge
buildSteps.detail: Add retrieval over vulnerability databases, patch notes and public write-ups so generated payloads match real product versions instead of being invented.

buildSteps.title: Map the attack surface
buildSteps.detail: Let the agent enumerate hosts, services, endpoints and exposed credentials, and assemble them into a graph of reachable paths.

buildSteps.title: Attempt and chain exploits
buildSteps.detail: The agent generates candidate payloads, tests them in the replica, keeps what works and combines single weaknesses into multi-step chains leading to a high-value target.

buildSteps.title: Verify on a clean snapshot
buildSteps.detail: Replay every claimed exploit from a fresh copy. Anything that cannot be reproduced is discarded, which removes most hallucinated findings.

buildSteps.title: Report and hand back to humans
buildSteps.detail: Produce findings with reproduction steps, evidence, severity and remediation advice, and route anything touching live systems to a human for approval before it is attempted.

prerequisites.tech: Large language models with reliable tool use
prerequisites.why: the agent must choose tools, parse messy output and hold a long multi-step plan without losing the thread.
running unknown exploits safely requires isolation and instant rollback, which virtual machines and containers already provide.
established scanners, fuzzers and exploitation frameworks do the mechanical work the agent orchestrates.
without standard scored challenges it is hard to tell a capable agent from one that writes convincing but false reports.
an agent that misreads its scope can cause real damage; allow-lists and kill switches are improving but not foolproof.

pathway.milestone: LLM assistants that speed up human penetration testers and automate reconnaissance plus known-vulnerability checks
pathway.unlocks: cheaper, more frequent security audits for organisations that could never afford constant manual testing.

pathway.milestone: agents that autonomously chain multi-stage exploits inside sandboxed replicas and prove each one by replay, as pushed by DARPA's AI Cyber Challenge
pathway.unlocks: verified, reproducible findings at machine speed with humans reviewing rather than hunting.

pathway.milestone: continuous red-teaming wired into software delivery pipelines, running under strict scope against staging environments
pathway.unlocks: vulnerabilities found and fixed before release instead of after a breach.

pathway.milestone: paired attack-and-defence agents that find and patch in the same loop, under audited guardrails and clear liability rules
pathway.unlocks: a security posture that improves faster than attackers can exploit it — provided the same capability is not turned loose without oversight.
